modules.name: Evaluation, Composition and Metabolic Management of Nephrolithiasis

topics.title: Nephrolithiasis: Pathogenesis, Crystal Types and Metabolic Evaluation
topics.book: Campbell-Walsh-Wein Urology 12e Ch 91-92 (Urinary Lithiasis: Etiology, Epidemiology, and Medical Management)

mustKnow.fact: Calcium oxalate stones account for approximately 70% to 80% of all urinary calculi, commonly initiating on Randall plaques in the renal papillary interstitium.
Uric acid calculi form in persistently acidic urine (pH less than 5.5) and are radiolucent on plain radiography but readily visualized on non-contrast computed tomography.
Struvite stones (magnesium ammonium phosphate and carbonate apatite) occur secondary to urease-producing organisms such as Proteus mirabilis and Klebsiella pneumoniae.
Cystine stones result from autosomal recessive mutations in SLC3A1 or SLC7A9 disrupting dibasic amino acid transport (cystine, ornithine, lysine, arginine: COLA).
Sodium nitroprusside (Brand test) detects urinary cystine above 75 mg/L producing a pathognomonic magenta or purple colour change.
Medical expulsive therapy using alpha-1 adrenergic antagonists (tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily) facilitates spontaneous passage of distal ureteral stones measuring 5 mm to 10 mm.
Hypocitraturia (urinary citrate less than 320 mg/day) is a major modifiable risk factor for calcium nephrolithiasis, managed with potassium citrate alkalinization to target pH 6.5 to 7.0.
Thiazide diuretics (chlorthalidone 25 mg or hydrochlorothiazide 25 to 50 mg daily) reduce hypercalciuria by enhancing proximal and distal tubular calcium reabsorption.

modules.name: Surgical Management: Shock Wave Lithotripsy and Ureteroscopy

topics.title: Shock Wave Lithotripsy and Flexible Ureteroscopy: Indications and Technique
topics.book: Campbell-Walsh-Wein Urology 12e Ch 93-94 (Surgical Management for Upper Urinary Tract Calculi)

mustKnow.fact: Extracorporeal shock wave lithotripsy (ESWL) achieves highest clearance for non-lower-pole renal calculi measuring less than 20 mm with attenuation under 1000 Hounsfield units.
ESWL is strictly contraindicated in pregnancy, uncorrected bleeding diathesis, active untreated urinary tract infection, and severe skeletal malformations.
Steinstrasse (stone street) refers to columns of unpassable stone fragments obstructing the ureter following ESWL, managed initially conservatively or via JJ stenting / URS.
Holmium:YAG laser (2100 nm wavelength) operates via photothermal mechanism with water absorption depth of 0.4 mm, ensuring safe fragmentation of all stone compositions.
Thulium fiber laser (TFL, 1940 nm wavelength) operates closer to water absorption peak with lower retropulsion, finer dust formation, and smaller fiber diameters (150 to 200 micrometres).
Ureteral access sheaths (typically 10/12F or 12/14F) reduce intrarenal pelvic pressures below 30 cmH2O during flexible ureterorenoscopy, mitigating pyelovenous backflow and sepsis.
Lower pole caliceal anatomy with infundibular angle less than 30 degrees, length over 30 mm, and width under 5 mm severely impedes stone fragment clearance after ESWL.
Postoperative ureteral stenting following uncomplicated ureteroscopy is discretionary for small pre-stented stones but strongly advised following dilatation, access sheath usage, or mucosal injury.

modules.name: Percutaneous Nephrolithotomy and Complex Staghorn Calculi

topics.title: Percutaneous Nephrolithotomy (PCNL): Access, Clearance and Complications
topics.book: Campbell-Walsh-Wein Urology 12e Ch 94 (Percutaneous Nephrolithotomy)

mustKnow.fact: Percutaneous nephrolithotomy (PCNL) represents the gold standard first-line treatment for renal calculi larger than 20 mm, staghorn calculi, and lower pole stones over 15 mm.
Renal access is typically obtained through the posterior calyx along the avascular line of Brodel (junction of anterior two-thirds and posterior third of the kidney).
Supracostal access above the 12th or 11th rib provides direct access to upper pole calculi but carries a 5% to 15% risk of hydrothorax or pneumothorax.
Mini-PCNL utilizes sheath sizes between 14F and 20F, reducing blood loss and parenchymal trauma compared to standard 24F to 30F tracts while enabling effective dusting.
Guy's stone score (Grades I to IV) and CROES nephrolithometric nomogram objectively stratify PCNL stone complexity and predict stone-free rates.
Severe arterial bleeding during or after PCNL that fails conservative balloon tamponade necessitates prompt selective transcatheter renal artery angioembolization.
Endoscopic combined intrarenal surgery (ECIRS) simultaneously employs retrograde flexible ureterorenoscopy and antegrade PCNL to maximize clearance of complex branched calculi.
Tubeless PCNL (omitting nephrostomy tube placement, leaving only a ureteral stent or catheter) is safe in uncomplicated procedures with complete stone clearance and minimal bleeding.

modules.name: Pelviureteric Junction Obstruction and Endopyelotomy

topics.title: Pelviureteric Junction (PUJ) Obstruction: Evaluation, Dismembered Pyeloplasty and Endourology
topics.book: Campbell-Walsh-Wein Urology 12e Ch 89 (Management of Upper Urinary Tract Obstruction)

mustKnow.fact: Pelviureteric junction (PUJ) obstruction in adults commonly arises from intrinsic aperistaltic segments or extrinsic compression by crossing lower pole accessory renal vessels (present in 30% to 50%).
Diuretic renography (99mTc-MAG3) confirms obstruction when clearance half-time (T1/2) after furosemide exceeds 20 minutes (equivocal between 10 and 20 minutes, normal under 10 minutes).
Anderson-Hynes dismembered pyeloplasty remains the gold standard definitive surgical repair with success rates exceeding 95% via open, laparoscopic, or robotic-assisted approaches.

Endopyelotomy involves a full-thickness posterolateral incision through the stenotic PUJ segment avoiding anterior crossing vessels, best suited for primary strictures under 1.5 cm with minimal hydronephrosis.
Fenger plasty and Y-V pyeloplasty (Foley) represent non-dismembered techniques indicated in secondary strictures or high ureteral insertions without crossing vessels.
Dietl crisis describes episodic severe flank pain, nausea, and vomiting caused by intermittent pelvic overdistension in walking or standing patients with movable kidneys (nephroptosis).
Whitaker test measures differential renal pelvic and bladder pressures during continuous antegrade perfusate infusion (10 mL/min); pressure gradient above 22 cmH2O diagnostic of obstruction.
Symptomatic PUJ obstruction in solitary functioning kidneys or with differential renal function deteriorating below 40% warrants prompt decompression or surgical correction.

modules.name: Ureteral Strictures, Boari Flap and Ureteral Reconstruction

topics.title: Ureteral Strictures and Injuries: Ureteroneocystostomy, Psoas Hitch and Boari Flap
topics.book: Campbell-Walsh-Wein Urology 12e Ch 89-90 (Upper Urinary Tract Trauma and Reconstruction)

mustKnow.fact: Distal ureteral strictures or transections within 4 cm to 5 cm of the ureterovesical junction are primarily repaired via non-refluxing or refluxing ureteroneocystostomy (ureteral reimplantation).
Psoas hitch mobilizes the bladder dome and anchors it to the tendon of the psoas minor or muscle belly, bridging distal ureteral gaps up to 6 cm to 8 cm without anastomotic tension.
Boari bladder flap creates a pedicled bladder wall flap rolled into a tube, bridging mid-to-lower ureteral defects up to 12 cm to 15 cm; base-to-apex flap ratio must be 2:1 to avoid ischemia.
Transureteroureterostomy (TUU) mobilizes the injured donor ureter across the retroperitoneum anterior to the aorta/vertebral spine to an end-to-side anastomosis with the recipient ureter.
TUU is strictly contraindicated in patients with urothelial carcinoma, chronic stone disease, retroperitoneal fibrosis, prior pelvic radiation, or severe bilateral ureteral disease.

Ileal ureter interposition utilizes an isoperistaltic segment of terminal ileum (sparing distal 15 cm) to bridge long, complex, pan-ureteral strictures in patients with serum creatinine below 2.0 mg/dL.
Buccal mucosal onlay grafting with robotic or laparoscopic omental wrap represents an effective technique for non-obliterative proximal and mid-ureteral strictures resistant to endourology.

Autotransplantation of the kidney into the iliac fossa with anastomosis to iliac vessels provides definitive salvage for extreme pan-ureteral loss when bladder flaps and bowel segments are unfeasible.

modules.name: Retroperitoneal Fibrosis and Extrinsic Ureteral Compression

topics.title: Retroperitoneal Fibrosis (Ormond Disease): Pathophysiology, Diagnosis and Ureterolysis
topics.book: Campbell-Walsh-Wein Urology 12e Ch 89 (Retroperitoneal Fibrosis and Extrinsic Compression)

mustKnow.fact: Retroperitoneal fibrosis (Ormond disease) is characterized by a fibro-inflammatory plaque centered over the lumbar spine and anterior aorta between L4 and S1, entrapping the ureters.
Up to 50% to 70% of idiopathic retroperitoneal fibrosis cases belong to the spectrum of systemic IgG4-related disease, with elevated serum IgG4 and dense IgG4-positive lymphoplasmacytic infiltrates.
Classical triad on intravenous or CT urography demonstrates medial deviation of the middle ureters, extrinsic ureteral narrowing at L4-L5, and proximal hydroureteronephrosis.
Malignant retroperitoneal fibrosis (due to lymphoma, sarcoma, or metastatic carcinoma) typically displaces the ureters laterally and expands cephalad above the renal vessels (L2).

First-line medical therapy for active non-malignant RPF consists of systemic corticosteroids (prednisolone 1 mg/kg/day for 4 weeks tapered over 6 to 9 months) with or without tamoxifen or mycophenolate.
Surgical ureterolysis involves liberating entrapped ureters from the fibrotic mantle, followed by lateral transposition into the peritoneal cavity (intraperitonealization) or omental wrapping.
Methysergide, ergotamine, beta-blockers, and hydralazine are well-documented pharmacologic culprits implicated in secondary drug-induced retroperitoneal fibrosis.
18F-FDG PET-CT scan accurately assesses inflammatory metabolic activity within the retroperitoneal plaque to monitor therapeutic response to corticosteroids and immunosuppressants.

modules.name: Renal Trauma: AAST Staging and Operative Management

topics.title: Renal Trauma: AAST Organ Injury Scale, Conservative Protocols and Exploration
topics.book: Campbell-Walsh-Wein Urology 12e Ch 90 (Upper Urinary Tract Trauma)

mustKnow.fact: Blunt mechanisms cause over 85% to 90% of renal trauma in civilian practice, with motor vehicle collisions and falls being the leading etiologies.

AAST Grade I involves subcapsular hematoma or contusion without laceration; Grade II involves non-expanding perirenal hematoma or cortical laceration less than 1 cm deep without collecting system rupture.
AAST Grade III represents cortical laceration extending greater than 1 cm deep without urinary extravasation or collecting system involvement.
AAST Grade IV features laceration involving the renal collecting system with urinary extravasation, segmental arterial/venous injury, or active bleeding contained within Gerota fascia.
AAST Grade V indicates a completely shattered kidney, avulsion of the renal hilum, or main renal artery or vein thrombosis devitalizing the organ.
Multiphasic contrast-enhanced CT with arterial, nephrographic, and delayed excretory phases (at 10 to 15 minutes) is the diagnostic imaging modality of choice in hemodynamically stable patients.

Absolute indications for renal surgical exploration include persistent hemodynamic instability unresponsive to resuscitation, expanding or pulsatile retroperitoneal hematoma, and Grade V vascular avulsion.
During surgical exploration, vascular control of the main renal artery and vein at the aorta and IVC prior to opening Gerota fascia significantly reduces nephrectomy rates.

modules.name: Lower Urinary Tract Trauma: Bladder and Urethral Rupture

topics.title: Lower Urinary Tract Trauma: Intraperitoneal vs Extraperitoneal Bladder Rupture and Posterior Urethral Injuries
topics.book: Campbell-Walsh-Wein Urology 12e Ch 133 (Genital and Lower Urinary Tract Trauma)

mustKnow.fact: Extraperitoneal bladder rupture (60% to 70% of bladder injuries) is strongly associated with pelvic fractures and is managed conservatively with large-bore urethral catheter drainage for 10 to 14 days.
Intraperitoneal bladder rupture (25% to 35%) occurs classically at the dome due to sudden compression of a distended bladder, mandating urgent formal operative repair with absorbable sutures.
Retrograde cystography or CT cystography with adequate bladder filling (at least 300 mL to 350 mL contrast instilled under gravity) is mandatory; underfilling produces false-negative results.

Posterior urethral disruption (membranous urethra, bulbomembranous junction) occurs in pelvic ring fractures, presenting with triad of blood at the external meatus, inability to void, and high-riding prostate.
Retrograde urethrography (RUG) must be performed prior to any attempt at urethral catheterization whenever urethral injury is clinically suspected.
Anterior urethral injuries most commonly result from blunt perineal straddle trauma compressing the bulbar urethra against the inferior pubic symphysis.

Colles fascia breach in anterior urethral trauma allows extravasated urine and blood to spread into the scrotum, penis, and anterior abdominal wall up to the clavicles, bounded by fascia lata at the thighs.

Management of complete posterior urethral distraction involves suprapubic cystostomy followed by delayed end-to-end anastomotic urethroplasty at 3 to 6 months, or early endoscopic primary realignment.

sections.name: Urological Oncology: Renal, Bladder, Prostate and Testicular Neoplasms

modules.name: Renal Cell Carcinoma: Histologic Subtypes and Hereditary Syndromes

topics.title: Renal Cell Carcinoma: Molecular Genetics, Subtypes and Hereditary Renal Syndromes
topics.book: Campbell-Walsh-Wein Urology 12e Ch 96-98 (Malignant Renal Tumors)

mustKnow.fact: Clear cell RCC accounts for 70% to 80% of renal malignancies, predominantly driven by 3p chromosomal loss and biallelic inactivation of the von Hippel-Lindau (VHL) tumor suppressor gene.
Loss of VHL leads to accumulation of hypoxia-inducible factors (HIF-1alpha and HIF-2alpha), causing overexpression of vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) and PDGF.
Papillary RCC (10% to 15%) is divided into Type 1 (MET proto-oncogene alterations on chromosome 7, basophilic cells) and Type 2 (fumarate hydratase deficiency, aggressive eosinophilic cells).
Chromophobe RCC (5%) arises from intercalated cells of the collecting duct, stains positive with Hale colloidal iron, and exhibits hypodiploidy with multiple chromosomal losses.
Birt-Hogg-Dube syndrome (FLCN gene mutation, folliculin) presents with cutaneous fibrofolliculomas, pulmonary cysts with spontaneous pneumothorax, and hybrid chromophobe/oncocytic renal tumours.
Hereditary leiomyomatosis and renal cell cancer (HLRCC) stems from fumarate hydratase (FH) mutations, characterized by cutaneous/uterine leiomyomas and aggressive solitary Type 2 papillary RCC.
Renal medullary carcinoma is a highly lethal malignancy exclusively seen in young patients with sickle cell trait, driven by loss of SMARCB1/INI1 expression.
Bosniak classification version 2019 categorizes cystic renal masses from I (benign simple) to IV (clearly malignant), with Bosniak III carrying a 50% and Bosniak IV an 85% malignancy risk.

modules.name: Renal Cell Carcinoma: Surgical and Systemic Management

topics.title: Renal Cell Carcinoma: Partial Nephrectomy, IVC Thrombus and Systemic Therapy
topics.book: Campbell-Walsh-Wein Urology 12e Ch 99-102 (Surgery for Renal Tumors and Systemic Therapy)

mustKnow.fact: Partial nephrectomy (nephron-sparing surgery) is the preferred standard of care for T1a renal masses (measuring 4 cm or less) and feasible T1b masses, preserving long-term renal function.
Warm ischemia time during partial nephrectomy should ideally remain under 20 to 25 minutes, or cold ischemia with ice slush under 35 minutes, to prevent irreversible acute tubular necrosis.
Renal cell carcinoma extends into the renal vein and inferior vena cava in 4% to 10% of cases, categorized by the Neves-Zincke staging from Level I (renal vein) to Level IV (above diaphragm/atrium).
Level IV IVC tumor thrombi require a multidisciplinary approach with cardiopulmonary bypass, deep hypothermic circulatory arrest, and transesophageal echocardiography monitoring.

IMDC (International Metastatic RCC Database Consortium) criteria risk-stratify metastatic RCC using 6 clinical factors: Karnofsky performance <80%, time from diagnosis to treatment <1 year, anemia, hypercalcemia, neutrophilia, thrombocytosis.
First-line systemic therapy for metastatic clear cell RCC in intermediate- and poor-risk disease combines dual immunotherapy (nivolumab plus ipilimumab) or a VEGFR-TKI plus anti-PD-1/PD-L1.
Adjuvant pembrolizumab for 1 year significantly prolongs disease-free survival in patients with resected high-risk clear cell renal cell carcinoma (KEYNOTE-564 trial).
Active surveillance or thermal ablation (cryoablation or radiofrequency ablation) represents an acceptable alternative for small renal masses under 3 cm in elderly, comorbid patients.

modules.name: Upper Tract Urothelial Carcinoma (UTUC)

topics.title: Upper Tract Urothelial Carcinoma: Diagnostic Stratification and Radical Nephroureterectomy
topics.book: Campbell-Walsh-Wein Urology 12e Ch 103-104 (Upper Tract Urothelial Carcinoma)

mustKnow.fact: Upper tract urothelial carcinoma (UTUC) accounts for 5% to 10% of all urothelial cancers, with 60% being invasive at presentation compared to 15% to 25% of bladder tumours.
Lynch syndrome (hereditary non-polyposis colorectal cancer, HNPCC) carries a 14- to 22-fold increased lifetime risk of UTUC, driven by germline DNA mismatch repair mutations (MSH2, MLH1, MSH6, PMS2).
Aristolochic acid nephropathy (Balkan endemic nephropathy and Chinese herb nephropathy) causes bilateral extensive UTUC characterized by distinct A:T to T:A transversions in TP53.
Radical nephroureterectomy (RNU) with en bloc excision of the ipsilateral bladder cuff represents the gold standard surgical therapy for high-risk UTUC.
Failure to completely resect the intramural ureter and bladder cuff results in a 30% to 50% recurrence rate in the ureteral stump or ipsilateral hemitrigone.

Kidney-sparing management (endoscopic laser ablation or segmental ureterectomy) is reserved for low-risk UTUC (unifocal, <2 cm, low grade, non-invasive) or imperative indications (solitary kidney, bilateral disease).
A single postoperative instillation of intravesical chemotherapy (mitomycin C or pirarubicin) within 2 to 10 days post-RNU reduces intravesical bladder recurrence by 40% to 50%.
Neoadjuvant platinum-based combination chemotherapy (gemcitabine plus cisplatin) improves overall survival and downstages locally advanced high-risk UTUC prior to nephroureterectomy.

modules.name: Non-Muscle Invasive Bladder Cancer (NMIBC) and BCG

topics.title: Non-Muscle Invasive Bladder Cancer: TURBT Technique, Risk Stratification and Intravesical BCG
topics.book: Campbell-Walsh-Wein Urology 12e Ch 135-136 (Non-Muscle-Invasive Bladder Cancer)

mustKnow.fact: Non-muscle invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) includes stages Ta (non-invasive papillary), T1 (invading lamina propria/subepithelial connective tissue), and Tis (carcinoma in situ, flat high grade).
Adequate transurethral resection of bladder tumour (TURBT) mandates inclusion of underlying detrusor muscle (muscularis propria) in the specimen to ensure accurate clinical staging.
A restaging second-look TURBT is strongly recommended within 2 to 6 weeks for all T1 tumours, high-grade tumours, or initial resections lacking detrusor muscle.
A single immediate postoperative instillation of intravesical chemotherapy (mitomycin C 40 mg or gemcitabine) within 24 hours of TURBT reduces recurrence by 35% in low-to-intermediate risk disease.

Intravesical Bacillus Calmette-Guerin (BCG) induction (weekly for 6 weeks) followed by 3-year maintenance (SWOG protocol: 3 weekly instillations at 3, 6, 12, 18, 24, 30, 36 months) is standard for high-risk NMIBC.

BCG sepsis represents a medical emergency presenting with fever and hemodynamic instability, requiring prompt cessation of BCG and therapy with isoniazid, rifampin, ethambutol, and high-dose corticosteroids.
BCG-unresponsive disease (persistent or recurrent high-grade Ta/T1 within 6 months or persistent CIS within 12 months of adequate BCG) is primarily managed with radical cystectomy.

Pembrolizumab (anti-PD-1) and nadofaragene firadenovec (adenoviral vector gene therapy) represent FDA-approved bladder-preserving therapies for BCG-unresponsive CIS patients ineligible for cystectomy.

modules.name: Muscle Invasive Bladder Cancer and Urinary Diversion

topics.title: Muscle-Invasive Bladder Cancer: Radical Cystectomy, Trimodal Therapy and Urinary Diversions
topics.book: Campbell-Walsh-Wein Urology 12e Ch 137-139 (Management and Surgery of Bladder Cancer)

mustKnow.fact: Neoadjuvant cisplatin-based combination chemotherapy (accelerated MVAC or gemcitabine plus cisplatin) confers a 5% to 8% absolute overall survival advantage at 5 years in muscle-invasive bladder cancer.

Standard radical cystectomy in men removes the bladder, prostate, seminal vesicles, distal ureters, and regional lymph nodes; in women (anterior pelvic exenteration) removes bladder, urethra, uterus, ovaries, anterior vaginal wall.
Bilateral pelvic lymph node dissection should clear at least 10 to 15 nodes, encompassing the external iliac, internal iliac (hypogastric), and obturator nodal packets.
Ileal conduit (Bricker diversion) isolates a 15 cm to 20 cm segment of terminal ileum (15 cm proximal to ileocecal valve), representing the most reliable incontinent urinary diversion.
Orthotopic neobladder (Studer, Hautmann) creates a low-pressure, high-capacity reservoir using 50 cm to 60 cm of detubularized ileum anastomosed directly to the native urethral stump.

Hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis is the classic electrolyte disturbance following ileal or colonic urinary diversions due to ammonium and chloride reabsorption in exchange for bicarbonate and sodium.

Trimodal bladder preservation therapy (maximal TURBT followed by concurrent chemoradiotherapy) achieves comparable survival in carefully selected patients with solitary T2 tumours without hydronephrosis or extensive CIS.

Enfortumab vedotin (antibody-drug conjugate targeting Nectin-4) combined with pembrolizumab significantly improves progression-free and overall survival as first-line therapy for locally advanced/metastatic urothelial cancer.

modules.name: Prostate Cancer: PSA Screening, mpMRI and Fusion Biopsy

topics.title: Prostate Cancer: PSA Kinetics, PI-RADS v2.1 mpMRI and Targeted Fusion Biopsy
topics.book: Campbell-Walsh-Wein Urology 12e Ch 148-150 (Prostate Cancer: Epidemiology, Biomarkers, and Biopsy)

mustKnow.fact: Prostate-specific antigen (PSA) is a kallikrein-like serine protease produced by prostatic epithelial cells; free-to-total PSA ratio under 10% to 15% strongly indicates increased malignancy risk.
Multiparametric MRI (mpMRI) evaluates the prostate using T2-weighted, diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI with ADC map), and dynamic contrast enhancement (DCE).
PI-RADS v2.1 scores lesions from 1 (very low) to 5 (very high likelihood of clinically significant cancer); DWI is the dominant sequence for peripheral zone and T2W for transition zone.
MRI-targeted transrectal or transperineal fusion biopsy combined with systematic 12-core biopsy significantly enhances detection of Grade Group 2 or higher cancers while reducing indolent diagnoses.
Transperineal biopsy approaches virtually eliminate post-biopsy sepsis and severe infectious complications compared to transrectal routes by avoiding rectal wall traversal.
International Society of Urological Pathology (ISUP) Grade Groups range from 1 (Gleason 3+3=6), 2 (Gleason 3+4=7), 3 (Gleason 4+3=7), 4 (Gleason 8), to 5 (Gleason 9-10).
PSA density (serum PSA divided by prostate volume on MRI/TRUS) exceeding 0.15 ng/mL/cc strongly correlates with clinically significant prostate cancer in gray-zone PSA levels (4 to 10 ng/mL).
Secondary biomarker tests including 4Kscore, Prostate Health Index (PHI), and PCA3 improve diagnostic specificity prior to repeat biopsy in patients with negative initial cores.

modules.name: Prostate Cancer: Staging, Prostatectomy and Systemic Therapy

topics.title: Prostate Cancer Management: Active Surveillance, Radical Prostatectomy, Radiotherapy and ADT
topics.book: Campbell-Walsh-Wein Urology 12e Ch 151-155 (Management of Localized and Advanced Prostate Cancer)

mustKnow.fact: Active surveillance represents the standard preferred strategy for low-risk prostate cancer (ISUP Grade Group 1, PSA <10 ng/mL, cT1c-cT2a), utilizing serial PSA, mpMRI, and protocol biopsies.
Robotic-assisted radical prostatectomy (RARP) dissects the neurovascular bundles between the prostatic fascia and levator fascia to preserve erectile function (nerve-sparing technique).
Biochemical recurrence after radical prostatectomy is defined as two consecutive post-operative PSA rises of 0.2 ng/mL or greater.
Biochemical recurrence after radiation therapy (Phoenix criteria) is defined as a PSA rise of 2.0 ng/mL or more above the post-treatment nadir value.
68Ga-PSMA or 18F-PSMA PET-CT scan exhibits superior sensitivity in localizing disease recurrence at very low PSA levels (even between 0.2 and 1.0 ng/mL).
Androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) achieves castrate testosterone levels (<50 ng/dL or <1.7 nmol/L) via LHRH agonists (leuprolide), LHRH antagonists (degarelix, relugolix), or bilateral orchiectomy.

Metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (mHSPC) standards of care incorporate doublet or triplet therapy: ADT plus androgen receptor signaling inhibitors (enzalutamide, apalutamide, abiraterone) +/- docetaxel.

Metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) harboring homologous recombination repair (HRR) mutations (BRCA1/2) demonstrates profound therapeutic response to PARP inhibitors (olaparib, rucaparib).

modules.name: Testicular Tumours, Biomarkers and Retroperitoneal Lymphadenectomy

topics.title: Testicular Germ Cell Tumours: Staging, Serum Markers and Retroperitoneal Lymph Node Dissection
topics.book: Campbell-Walsh-Wein Urology 12e Ch 76-78 (Neoplasms of the Testis and Surgery)

mustKnow.fact: Radical inguinal orchiectomy with high ligation of the spermatic cord at the internal inguinal ring is mandatory; scrotal violation or trans-scrotal biopsy is strictly contraindicated.
Serum tumor markers include alpha-fetoprotein (AFP, half-life 5 to 7 days), beta-human chorionic gonadotropin (beta-hCG, half-life 24 to 36 hours), and lactate dehydrogenase (LDH).
AFP is never elevated in pure seminoma or pure choriocarcinoma; elevation of AFP in a presumed seminoma mandates management as a non-seminomatous germ cell tumour (NSGCT).
Primary lymphatic drainage of the right testis is into interaortocaval lymph nodes, whereas the left testis drains primarily into para-aortic lymph nodes near the left renal hilum.
Nerve-sparing retroperitoneal lymph node dissection (RPLND) meticulously preserves postganglionic sympathetic fibers of the hypogastric plexus (L1 to L3) to maintain antegrade ejaculation.

Post-chemotherapy residual retroperitoneal masses in NSGCT measuring greater than 1 cm with normalized tumor markers mandate complete surgical excision (RPLND) due to high teratoma/viable cancer risk.
Post-chemotherapy seminoma residual masses under 3 cm are managed with surveillance; masses >=3 cm require 18F-FDG PET-CT scan at least 6 to 8 weeks post-chemotherapy to assess metabolic activity.

IGCCCG (International Germ Cell Cancer Collaborative Group) stratifies metastatic germ cell tumours into good, intermediate, and poor prognostic groups based on primary site, metastases, and marker nadir.

sections.name: BPH, Lower Urinary Tract Dysfunction, Incontinence and Urodynamics

modules.name: Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia: Pathophysiology and Medical Therapy

topics.title: Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia: Etiology, Natural History and Medical Management
topics.book: Campbell-Walsh-Wein Urology 12e Ch 143-145 (Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia: Physiology and Nonsurgical Management)

mustKnow.fact: Benign prostatic hyperplasia originates exclusively in the transition zone of the prostate, driven by intracellular dihydrotestosterone (DHT) binding androgen receptors with 5-fold higher affinity than testosterone.
5-alpha reductase converts circulating testosterone to DHT; Type 2 isoenzyme is predominantly expressed in prostatic stromal cells, while Type 1 is expressed in liver and skin.

Alpha-1 adrenergic antagonists (tamsulosin 0.4 mg, silodosin 8 mg) relax prostatic smooth muscle via alpha-1A selectivity, providing rapid symptomatic relief within days without altering prostate size.
5-alpha reductase inhibitors (finasteride 5 mg, dutasteride 0.5 mg) reduce prostate volume by 20% to 25%, reduce PSA by 50%, and prevent urinary retention/surgery in prostates larger than 30 cc.
Combination therapy with an alpha-blocker and 5-ARI (MTOPS and CombAT trials) is superior to monotherapy in arresting disease progression, reducing acute retention, and decreasing surgical necessity.
Phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitors (tadalafil 5 mg daily) improve lower urinary tract symptoms and concurrent erectile dysfunction via upregulation of cGMP and smooth muscle relaxation.
Intraoperative floppy iris syndrome (IFIS) occurs during cataract surgery in patients exposed to alpha-1A antagonists (notably tamsulosin), requiring preoperative notification to the ophthalmologist.

Absolute indications for surgical intervention in BPH comprise refractory urinary retention, recurrent gross hematuria, recurrent UTIs, secondary bladder calculi, and renal failure due to bilateral hydronephrosis.

modules.name: BPH Surgical Interventions: TURP, Laser Enucleation and MIST

topics.title: Surgical Management of BPH: Monopolar/Bipolar TURP, HoLEP, ThuLEP and Minimally Invasive Therapies
topics.book: Campbell-Walsh-Wein Urology 12e Ch 146-147 (Endoscopic and Surgical Management of BPH)

mustKnow.fact: Monopolar TURP utilizes non-conductive, hypoosmolar irrigation fluid (1.5% glycine or sorbitol/mannitol), posing risk of transurethral resection (TUR) syndrome.

TUR syndrome results from excessive systemic absorption of hypoosmolar glycine, presenting with acute hypervolemic hyponatremia, encephalopathy, visual disturbances, and bradycardia; managed with 3% hypertonic saline.
Bipolar TURP operates in normal isotonic saline (0.9% NaCl), generating localized plasma corona to resect tissue while completely eliminating the risk of dilutional hyponatremia/TUR syndrome.
Holmium laser enucleation of the prostate (HoLEP) dissects entire prostatic adenoma along the surgical capsule regardless of prostate gland size, followed by mechanical tissue morcellation.
Thulium laser enucleation (ThuLEP) provides precise continuous-wave cutting and superior coagulation with minimal coagulation depth (0.1 to 0.2 mm), safe for patients on oral anticoagulation.
Prostatic urethral lift (UroLift) uses transprostatic suture implants to retract obstructing lateral lobes without thermal injury, completely preserving ejaculatory and erectile function.
Water vapor thermal therapy (Rezum) injects radiofrequency-generated convective steam (103 deg C) into transition zone tissue and median lobe, inducing cellular necrosis and subsequent resorption.

Simple prostatectomy (open, laparoscopic, or robotic-assisted Freyer transvesical / Millin retropubic) is reserved for massive benign adenomas exceeding 80 cc to 100 cc when enucleation expertise is unavailable.

modules.name: Urodynamics and Neurogenic Bladder Dysfunction

topics.title: Urodynamics Principles, Neuropathic Bladder Dysfunction and Autonomic Dysreflexia
topics.book: Campbell-Walsh-Wein Urology 12e Ch 111-114 (Urodynamic Evaluation and Neurogenic Bladder)

mustKnow.fact: Detrusor pressure (Pdet) during filling cystometry is calculated continuously by subtracting intra-abdominal pressure (Pabd, via rectal balloon) from total intravesical pressure (Pves).
Normal bladder compliance is defined as change in volume divided by change in detrusor pressure (Delta-V / Delta-Pdet), with values below 12 to 20 mL/cmH2O indicating dangerously low compliance.
Detrusor leak point pressure (DLPP) exceeding 40 cmH2O in neurogenic patients is strongly predictive of upper urinary tract deterioration, hydronephrosis, and secondary renal damage.
Suprapontine lesions (stroke, Parkinson disease) typically produce detrusor overactivity with coordinated sphincter relaxation, maintaining normal voiding synergy.

Suprasacral spinal lesions (cervical/thoracic spinal trauma above T6) cause detrusor-sphincter dyssynergia (DSD), wherein involuntary detrusor contraction coincides with involuntary external urethral sphincter closure.

Autonomic dysreflexia occurs in spinal cord lesions at or above T6, triggered by bladder overdistension, presenting with paroxysmal life-threatening hypertension, severe headache, bradycardia, and diaphoresis.
Sacral and infrasacral lesions (conus medullaris, cauda equina, pelvic plexus surgery) lead to an acontractile detrusor with low bladder compliance and loss of voluntary sphincter control.
Clean intermittent catheterization (CIC) introduced by Lapides remains the cornerstone gold standard management for patients with incomplete bladder emptying and neuropathic retention.

modules.name: Urinary Incontinence: Classification and Surgical Correction

topics.title: Urinary Incontinence: Stress, Urgency, Midurethral Slings and Artificial Urinary Sphincter
topics.book: Campbell-Walsh-Wein Urology 12e Ch 112-113, 115 (Urinary Incontinence and Pelvic Prolapse)

mustKnow.fact: Stress urinary incontinence (SUI) results from urethral hypermobility (loss of pelvic support) or intrinsic sphincter deficiency (ISD, abdominal leak point pressure <60 cmH2O, MUCP <20 cmH2O).
Midurethral synthetic slings (retropubic TVT and transobturator TOT) represent the standard surgical treatment for female stress urinary incontinence with urethral hypermobility.
Autologous rectus fascial pubovaginal sling is indicated in complicated female SUI, recurrent incontinence, severe ISD, or prior urethral mesh erosion/diverticulum.

Overactive bladder (OAB) is managed in a stepped algorithmic manner: behavioral therapy first, followed by antimuscarinics (solifenacin, oxybutynin) or beta-3 agonists (mirabegron 50 mg, vibegron 75 mg).
Third-line therapies for refractory OAB comprise intra-detrusor onabotulinumtoxinA injections (100 units), sacral neuromodulation (InterStim), and percutaneous tibial nerve stimulation (PTNS).
Artificial urinary sphincter (AUS, AMS 800) is the definitive gold standard surgical correction for severe post-prostatectomy male stress incontinence secondary to sphincter incompetence.
Male slings (transobturator or quadratic adjustable) are suited for mild-to-moderate male stress incontinence (1 to 3 pads daily) in patients with preserved residual sphincter contractility.
Burch colposuspension suspends the paravaginal endopelvic fascia to Cooper's iliopectineal ligament via open or laparoscopic access, effective for anatomical urethral hypermobility.

modules.name: Pelvic Organ Prolapse and Genitourinary Fistulae

topics.title: Pelvic Organ Prolapse, POP-Q Staging, Vesicovaginal and Ureterovaginal Fistulae
topics.book: Campbell-Walsh-Wein Urology 12e Ch 112, 115 (Pelvic Prolapse and Urogenital Fistulae)

mustKnow.fact: POP-Q (Pelvic Organ Prolapse Quantification) system uses the hymenal ring as zero reference plane to objectively stage anterior, apical, and posterior vaginal compartment descent.
Abdominal or robotic sacrocolpopexy using lightweight polypropylene mesh anchored to the anterior longitudinal ligament of the sacrum (S1) is the gold standard repair for apical prolapse.

Vesicovaginal fistula (VVF) in developing countries predominantly results from prolonged obstructed labor (ischemic necrosis), whereas in developed nations 80% to 90% follow iatrogenic gynecologic surgery (abdominal hysterectomy).

Double dye test differentiates VVF from ureterovaginal fistula: oral phenazopyridine (turns urine orange) combined with intravesical methylene blue instillation; blue tampon stain confirms VVF, orange confirms ureteral fistula.
Latzko partial colpocleisis provides high cure rates (>95%) for supratrigonal post-hysterectomy VVFs via vaginal approach without disrupting ureteral orifices or bladder neck.
Transvesical or transabdominal O'Conor technique bisects the bladder vertically down to the fistulous tract, mobilizing bladder flaps with vascularized interposition grafts (omental flap).
Martius labial fibrofatty flap provides vascularized interposition tissue during transvaginal repair of complex, recurrent, or post-radiation vesicovaginal and urethrovaginal fistulae.
Radiation-induced VVFs require delayed surgical repair (at least 6 to 12 months following radiation cessation) and mandatory vascularized tissue flap transfer to ensure viable healing.

modules.name: Interstitial Cystitis / Bladder Pain Syndrome

topics.title: Interstitial Cystitis / Bladder Pain Syndrome (IC/BPS): Hunner Lesions, Pathophysiology and Multimodal Therapy
topics.book: Campbell-Walsh-Wein Urology 12e Ch 57 (Interstitial Cystitis/Bladder Pain Syndrome)

mustKnow.fact: Interstitial cystitis/bladder pain syndrome (IC/BPS) is defined as chronic pelvic pain, pressure, or discomfort related to the bladder, accompanied by lower urinary tract symptoms for over 6 weeks without infection.

Hunner lesions (Hunner ulcers) are identified in 5% to 10% of patients on cystoscopy, presenting as circumscribed erythematous mucosal areas with radiating capillaries that tear and bleed with hydrodistension.
Glomerulations (petechial submucosal hemorrhages appearing after low-pressure hydrodistension) are non-specific and no longer considered mandatory or pathognomonic for IC/BPS diagnosis.
Disruption of the protective urothelial glycosaminoglycan (GAG) layer allows urinary solutes (potassium) to penetrate the submucosa, activating sensory C-fibers and mast cells.

Pentosan polysulfate sodium (PPS, Elmiron 100 mg three times daily) is the only oral FDA-approved disease-specific drug; long-term use requires baseline and periodic ophthalmologic screening for maculopathy.
Amitriptyline (tricyclic antidepressant, 25 to 75 mg nightly) provides effective symptom relief via anticholinergic, antihistaminic, and central pain modulating pathways.
Endoscopic fulguration (electrocautery, laser ablation) or triamcinolone submucosal injection directly into Hunner lesions provides rapid, profound symptom remission in ulcer-type IC/BPS.

Intravesical instillation therapies (dimethyl sulfoxide [DMSO], heparin, lidocaine, sodium hyaluronate) directly restore the urothelial barrier and attenuate peripheral C-fiber neurogenic inflammation.

modules.name: Nocturia, Nocturnal Polyuria and Circadian Bladder Control

topics.title: Nocturia and Nocturnal Polyuria: Diagnosis, Frequency-Volume Charts and Desmopressin Therapy
topics.book: Campbell-Walsh-Wein Urology 12e Ch 110-111 (Physiology of Bladder Storage and Nocturia)

mustKnow.fact: Nocturia is defined by the ICS as waking to void one or more times during the main sleep period, with each void preceded and followed by sleep.

Nocturnal polyuria is objectively established on a 3-day frequency-volume chart when nocturnal bladder output exceeds 20% to 33% of 24-hour total urine volume (nocturnal polyuria index >0.20 to >0.33 by age).
Global 24-hour polyuria is defined as total urinary output exceeding 40 mL/kg over 24 hours (roughly >2.8 to 3.0 L/day), caused by diabetes mellitus, diabetes insipidus, or primary polydipsia.
Nocturnal polyuria in elderly adults commonly stems from loss of circadian arginine vasopressin (AVP) secretion, congestive heart failure, venous insufficiency, or obstructive sleep apnea.
Desmopressin (oral lyophilisate / sublingual melt 25 to 50 mcg for men, 12.5 to 25 mcg for women) selectively activates renal V2 receptors in the collecting duct, reducing nocturnal urine production.
Serum sodium monitoring is mandatory prior to initiating desmopressin, at 1 week, 1 month, and periodically thereafter, to prevent severe dilutional hyponatremia, especially in adults over 65 years.
Loop diuretics (furosemide 20 to 40 mg) administered 6 hours prior to bedtime promote fluid mobilization from lower extremity edema during daytime hours, effectively curbing nocturnal volume shifts.

Reduced nocturnal bladder capacity (nocturia index >1.5 with nocturnal maximum voided volume < functional daytime capacity) distinguishes bladder-storage etiologies from purely systemic polyuric mechanisms.

modules.name: Catheterization, CAUTI and Urological Drainage Systems

topics.title: Lower Urinary Tract Drainage: Urethral Catheterization, Suprapubic Cystostomy and CAUTI Prevention
topics.book: Campbell-Walsh-Wein Urology 12e Ch 11-12 (Catheterization and Drainage)

mustKnow.fact: Catheter-associated urinary tract infection (CAUTI) develops via extraluminal bacterial biofilm migration along the catheter-urethral mucosal interface or intraluminal ascension following drainage bag contamination.
Risk of bacteriuria increases cumulatively by 3% to 7% per day of indwelling urethral catheterization, approaching nearly 100% by 30 days of continuous drainage.

Suprapubic cystostomy is indicated for acute urinary retention where urethral catheterization is impossible or contraindicated (acute bacterial prostatitis, traumatic urethral disruption, severe urethral stricture).
Percutaneous suprapubic puncture must only be undertaken when the urinary bladder is palpably distended or accurately localized under real-time ultrasound to prevent fatal small bowel perforation.

Coude-tip (Tiemann) catheters feature a 45-degree anteriorly curved tip designed specifically to navigate over elevated bladder necks and enlarged prostate median lobes without creating false passages.

Catheter balloon deflation failure is managed systematically: cut the inflation arm, pass a fine stylet through the channel, transabdominal ultrasound-guided puncture, or transrectal/transvaginal needle aspiration.
Silver alloy-coated and nitrofurazone-impregnated catheters reduce short-term asymptomatic bacteriuria in hospital settings but have not consistently reduced clinical sepsis or overall mortality.

Bladder spasms related to indwelling catheter irritation are treated with anticholinergic medications (solifenacin, oxybutynin) or beta-3 agonists, alongside verifying catheter balloon position and drainage patency.

sections.name: Urethral Strictures, Andrology, Male Infertility and Sexual Medicine

modules.name: Anterior Urethral Strictures and Substitution Urethroplasty

topics.title: Anterior Urethral Strictures: Buccal Mucosa Urethroplasty, EPA and Lichen Sclerosus
topics.book: Campbell-Walsh-Wein Urology 12e Ch 80, 82 (Surgery of the Penis and Urethra)

mustKnow.fact: Bulbar urethral strictures measuring less than 2 cm without extensive spongiofibrosis are primarily repaired via transecting or non-transecting excision and primary anastomosis (EPA) with success >90%.
Strictures longer than 2 cm or involving the penile urethra require substitution urethroplasty, with autologous oral buccal mucosal graft (BMG) representing the gold standard graft material.
Dorsal onlay graft (Barbagli technique) fixes the buccal mucosal graft directly to the tunica albuginea of the corpora cavernosa, providing a stable, highly vascular bed with excellent graft take.
Ventral onlay graft is suitable in the proximal bulbar urethra where robust overlying spongiosum allows tension-free coverage, avoiding mobilization of dorsal neurovascular bundles.

Lichen sclerosus (balanitis xerotica obliterans, BZO) is a chronic inflammatory dermatosis causing dense panurethral and meatal strictures; genital skin flaps are strictly contraindicated due to disease recurrence.
Penile urethral strictures must never be treated with excision and primary anastomosis due to chordee formation and penile shortening; substitution urethroplasty (BMG) is mandatory.

Two-stage urethroplasty (Johanson or Bracka technique) using free grafts is indicated for complex re-operative strictures, failed hypospadias repairs (hypospadias cripples), and severe lichen sclerosus.
Direct vision internal urethrotomy (DVIU) has a definitive long-term curative success rate under 10% to 20% when repeated; repeating DVIU beyond one failure is strongly discouraged by guidelines.

modules.name: Pelvic Fracture Urethral Distraction Defects

topics.title: Pelvic Fracture Urethral Injuries: Progressive Perineal Anastomotic Repair (Webster Technique)
topics.book: Campbell-Walsh-Wein Urology 12e Ch 82, 133 (Posterior Urethral Reconstruction)

mustKnow.fact: Pelvic fracture urethral distraction defects (PFUDD) involve avulsion of the membranous urethra at the bulbomembranous junction, with intervening fibrous scar displacing the prostatic apex.
Preoperative evaluation requires simultaneous retrograde urethrography (RUG) and voiding cystourethrography (VCUG) through a suprapubic catheter to define defect length and bladder neck competence.
Webster elaborated perineal approach uses a standardized 4-step progressive elaboration to achieve tension-free mucosa-to-mucosa anastomotic repair.
Step 1 of Webster's approach comprises extensive mobilization of the anterior bulbar urethra from the corpus cavernosum forward to the penoscrotal junction, gaining 2 cm to 3 cm of length.
Step 2 involves complete crural separation by sharply dividing the midline intercrural septum between the divergent corpora cavernosa, bridging an additional 1 cm to 2 cm gap.
Step 3 involves inferior pubectomy, resecting a wedge of the inferior pubic symphysis to create a straight bony trough for the mobilizing urethra directly to the prostatic apex.
Step 4 (supracrural rerouting) detaches the mobilised urethra and routes it around the lateral aspect of the right or left corporal body directly through the obturator foramen.
Primary open realignment at initial pelvic trauma carries substantial risks of hemorrhage, neurovascular injury, and erectile dysfunction, and is reserved for select hemodynamically stable patients.

modules.name: Erectile Dysfunction and Penile Prosthesis Implantation

topics.title: Erectile Dysfunction: Nitric Oxide Pathway, Pharmacotherapy and Penile Prosthesis Implantation
topics.book: Campbell-Walsh-Wein Urology 12e Ch 68-69 (Erectile Dysfunction: Pathophysiology and Management)

mustKnow.fact: Penile erection is initiated by parasympathetic non-adrenergic non-cholinergic (NANC) nerve release of nitric oxide (NO), stimulating guanylate cyclase to synthesize cyclic GMP (cGMP).

Intracellular cGMP dephosphorylates myosin light chains, causing trabecular cavernosal smooth muscle relaxation, arterial inflow, and passive compression of subtunical emissary veins against the tunica albuginea (veno-occlusive mechanism).

PDE-5 inhibitors (sildenafil 50-100 mg, tadalafil 10-20 mg) prevent cGMP breakdown; co-administration with nitrates (nitroglycerin) is absolutely contraindicated due to catastrophic life-threatening hypotension.
Intracavernosal injection therapy utilizes alprostadil (PGE1), papaverine, and phentolamine (Trimix), representing second-line medical therapy with success exceeding 85%.

Three-piece inflatable penile prosthesis (IPP) comprising dual intracorporal cylinders, scrotal control pump, and preperitoneal fluid reservoir provides highest patient/partner satisfaction rates (>95%).
Prosthetic device infection (1% to 2% in primary non-diabetic cases, higher in revisions) is most commonly caused by Staphylococcus epidermidis and gram-negative bacilli.
Mulcahy salvage salvage protocol for infected penile prosthesis involves immediate device explantation, multi-solution antiseptic antibiotic washout, and immediate reimplantation of a new prosthesis.

Penile duplex Doppler ultrasonography demonstrates arterial insufficiency if peak systolic velocity (PSV) is <25 cm/s, and veno-occlusive dysfunction if end-diastolic velocity (EDV) is >5 cm/s with resistive index <0.8.

modules.name: Priapism: Ischemic, Non-Ischemic and Shunt Procedures

topics.title: Priapism: Ischemic vs Non-Ischemic Classifications, Cavernosal Aspiration and Shunts
topics.book: Campbell-Walsh-Wein Urology 12e Ch 70 (Priapism)

mustKnow.fact: Ischemic (low-flow, veno-occlusive) priapism is a painful medical compartment emergency marked by rigid corpora, absent cavernosal arterial inflow, and progressive cavernosal acidosis and hypoxia.
Cavernosal blood gas in ischemic priapism shows profound acidosis and hypoxia: pH <7.25, pO2 <30 mmHg, pCO2 >60 mmHg (identical to ischemic venous blood).
Non-ischemic (high-flow, arterial) priapism is typically painless and non-rigid, resulting from blunt perineal trauma creating an uncontrolled cavernosal arteriolar-sinusoidal fistula.

Initial therapy for ischemic priapism involves corporal aspiration and irrigation with saline followed by intracavernosal injection of phenylephrine (alpha-1 agonist, 100 to 500 mcg/mL every 3 to 5 minutes).
Distal percutaneous shunts (Winter, Ebbehoj) create a communication between the glans penis and corpora cavernosa using a large-bore biopsy needle or scalpel.
Distal open operative shunts (Al-Ghorab, Burnett) excise a 5 mm circular or elliptical core of distal tunica albuginea through the glans to re-establish outflow.
Proximal surgical shunts include Quackels shunt (corporospongiosal anastomosis at the perineum) and Grayhack shunt (saphenous vein-to-corpus cavernosum anastomosis).

Ischemic priapism persisting beyond 36 to 48 hours causes complete cavernosal smooth muscle necrosis and fibrosis; immediate insertion of a penile prosthesis resolves priapism and prevents penile shortening.

modules.name: Peyronie Disease and Penile Curvature

topics.title: Peyronie Disease: Pathobiology, Plaque Incision/Grafting and Nesbit Plication
topics.book: Campbell-Walsh-Wein Urology 12e Ch 71 (Peyronie Disease)

mustKnow.fact: Peyronie disease is an acquired fibroproliferative disorder of the tunica albuginea resulting from microvascular trauma during intercourse in genetically susceptible men, causing fibrous collagenous plaques.

The natural history comprises an active/inflammatory phase (painful erections, dynamic evolving curvature, soft palpable plaque) and a chronic/stable phase (pain resolved, stable curvature >3 to 6 months, calcification).
Collagenase Clostridium histolyticum (CCH, Xiaflex) is the only FDA-approved intralesional therapy for stable palpable plaques with curvature between 30 and 90 degrees.

Nesbit corporoplasty and tunica albuginea plication (TAP) shorten the convex (long) side of the penis opposite the plaque; indicated for curves <60 degrees without hourglass defect, causing modest length loss.

Plaque incision and grafting (PIG) lengthens the contracted concave side of the penis; indicated for severe curvature >60 degrees, short penis, or hourglass deformity in men with normal baseline erectile function.
Grafting materials for PIG include autologous tissues (saphenous vein, fascia lata, buccal mucosa) or xenografts/allografts (porcine small intestinal submucosa, pericardium).

Penile prosthesis implantation combined with manual modeling or plaque incision is the treatment of choice for Peyronie disease in patients with concurrent erectile dysfunction unresponsive to pharmacotherapy.
Surgical intervention is strictly contraindicated during the active inflammatory phase of Peyronie disease while the deformity is dynamically evolving.

modules.name: Male Infertility: Azoospermia, Genetics and Varicocelectomy

topics.title: Male Infertility: Evaluation, Obstructive vs Non-Obstructive Azoospermia and Microscopic Varicocelectomy
topics.book: Campbell-Walsh-Wein Urology 12e Ch 66-67 (Male Infertility: Evaluation and Surgical Management)

mustKnow.fact: Semen analysis normal reference parameters (WHO 6th edition, 2021): volume >=1.4 mL, total motility >=42%, progressive motility >=30%, sperm concentration >=16 million/mL, normal forms >=4%.

Obstructive azoospermia (OA) presents with normal testis size, normal serum FSH, and dilated epididymides; non-obstructive azoospermia (NOA) presents with small atrophic testes and elevated serum FSH.

Congenital bilateral absence of the vas deferens (CBAVD) is identified in >95% of patients with mutations in the CFTR (cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator) gene; genetic counseling is mandatory.

Y-chromosome microdeletions in the AZF (azoospermia factor) region on Yq11 involve AZFa, AZFb, and AZFc; complete deletions of AZFa or AZFb predict 0% sperm retrieval, whereas AZFc yields successful TESE in 50%.
Klinefelter syndrome (47,XXY) is the most common genetic cause of non-obstructive azoospermia, featuring hypergonadotropic hypogonadism, small firm testes, and gynecomastia.

Microscopic subinguinal varicocelectomy achieves highest pregnancy rates and lowest recurrence (<1%) and hydrocele rates by preserving internal spermatic arteries and lymphatics under 10x-15x magnification.
Microdissection testicular sperm extraction (micro-TESE) uses operative microscopy to isolate dilated, opaque seminiferous tubules in NOA, achieving sperm retrieval rates of 40% to 50%.

Microsurgical vasoepididymostomy (intussusception end-to-side technique) is indicated for epididymal obstruction in OA, utilizing 10-0 and 11-0 sutures to anastomose vas lumen to a single epididymal tubule.

modules.name: Penile Carcinoma: Staging and Inguinal Node Dissection

topics.title: Penile Cancer: HPV Associations, Staging, Organ-Sparing Surgery and Inguinal Lymphadenectomy
topics.book: Campbell-Walsh-Wein Urology 12e Ch 79, 81 (Tumors of the Penis and Inguinal Node Dissection)

mustKnow.fact: Squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) accounts for >95% of penile malignancies, with high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV genotypes 16 and 18) implicated in 30% to 50% of cases.
Premalignant penile lesions comprise erythroplasia of Queyrat (involving glans and prepuce) and Bowen disease (involving penile shaft), both representing carcinoma in situ (Tis).

Organ-sparing surgeries (wide local excision, glansectomy with skin graft, Mohs micrographic surgery) provide excellent oncologic control for low-risk T1 lesions with clear surgical margins of 3 mm to 5 mm.
Partial penectomy with spatulated neo-meatus is indicated for invasive T2 tumours where a functional penile stump enabling upright micturition (at least 2 cm to 3 cm) can be preserved.
Inguinal lymph node dissection (ILND) is mandatory for intermediate- and high-risk primary tumours (T1G3, T2 or higher), as clinical palpation misses occult nodal micrometastases in 20% to 25%.
Dynamic sentinel lymph node biopsy (DSNB) utilizing 99mTc-nanocolloid and patent blue or ICG provides accurate nodal staging while reducing the 30% to 50% wound morbidity of full ILND.
Bilateral pelvic lymphadenectomy is indicated when two or more inguinal lymph nodes are histologically positive, or in the presence of extracapsular nodal extension (pN2/pN3).
Neoadjuvant combination chemotherapy with paclitaxel, ifosfamide, and cisplatin (TIP regimen) is recommended for fixed, ulcerated, or bulky inguinal nodal metastases prior to consolidation surgery.

modules.name: Benign Scrotal Conditions: Hydrocele, Spermatocele and Torsion

topics.title: Acute Scrotum and Benign Scrotal Disorders: Testicular Torsion, Epididymo-orchitis and Hydrocele
topics.book: Campbell-Walsh-Wein Urology 12e Ch 63, 76 (Genital and Scrotal Disorders)

mustKnow.fact: Testicular torsion is a surgical emergency caused by abnormal high insertion of the tunica vaginalis (bell-clapper deformity), allowing intravaginal rotation of the spermatic cord.
The critical golden window for surgical detorsion and salvage is within 6 hours of symptom onset (salvage >90%), dropping precipitously to under 10% after 24 hours.

Manual detorsion is performed in an open-book fashion (rotating right testis counter-clockwise and left testis clockwise as viewed from foot of bed); bilateral orchidopexy is mandatory regardless of salvage.
Torsion of the appendix testis (hydatid of Morgagni) presents with blue dot sign in the upper pole; managed conservatively unless diagnosis is equivocal.
Acute epididymo-orchitis demonstrates positive Prehn sign (pain relief with scrotal elevation) and hypervascularity with low resistive index on color Doppler ultrasound.
In men under 35 years, epididymitis is predominantly caused by sexually transmitted Chlamydia trachomatis and Neisseria gonorrhoeae; in men over 35 years, by coliform enteric pathogens (E. coli).
Hydrocele is abnormal accumulation of serous fluid between visceral and parietal layers of the tunica vaginalis, surgically treated via Jaboulay eversion or Lord plication techniques.
Spermatocele represents a benign retention cyst of the efferent ductules or epididymis containing non-viable spermatozoa, distinct from the testis and treated via spermatocelectomy if symptomatic.

sections.name: Paediatric Urology, Congenital Anomalies and DSD

modules.name: Hypospadias and Congenital Penile Anomalies

topics.title: Hypospadias: Embryology, Tubularized Incised Plate (Snodgrass) and Staged Urethroplasty
topics.book: Campbell-Walsh-Wein Urology 12e Ch 42-43 (Hypospadias and Penile Reconstruction)

mustKnow.fact: Hypospadias is characterized by a triad of an abnormally proximal ventral urethral meatus, ventral penile curvature (chordee), and a hooded dorsal prepuce.
Neonatal circumcision is strictly contraindicated in boys born with hypospadias because the preputial skin is critically required for future surgical reconstruction.
Optimal timing for hypospadias repair is between 6 and 18 months of age, prior to the development of genital awareness and memory.
Tubularized incised plate urethroplasty (TIP, Snodgrass repair) makes a midline relaxing incision along the urethral plate to tubularize distal and mid-shaft hypospadias without tissue grafting.
Mathieu perimeatal-based flap repairs distal defects with a flat, non-pliable plate, flipping a ventral shaft skin flap over the urethral defect.

Severe proximal hypospadias with severe chordee (>30 degrees after penile degloving) requires urethral plate transection and a two-stage repair (Bracka technique using inner preputial or buccal graft).
Urethrocutaneous fistula (5% to 15%) is the most common postoperative complication, minimized by interposition of a vascularized dartos or tunica vaginalis barrier layer.
Urethral meatal stenosis is avoided in the Snodgrass repair by terminating tubularization 2 mm to 3 mm proximal to the tip of the glans and avoiding distal overclosure.

modules.name: Cryptorchidism and Undescended Testis

topics.title: Cryptorchidism: Evaluation, Fowler-Stephens Orchiopexy and Malignancy Risk
topics.book: Campbell-Walsh-Wein Urology 12e Ch 44 (Cryptorchidism and Testicular Maldescent)

mustKnow.fact: Cryptorchidism affects approximately 3% of full-term and up to 30% of premature male neonates, with spontaneous descent rarely occurring after 3 to 6 months of age.
Definitive surgical orchidopexy should be performed between 6 and 12 months of age, and completed by 18 months, to preserve spermatogenesis and Leydig cell architecture.
Diagnostic laparoscopy is the gold standard imaging and intervention for non-palpable testes, identifying blind-ending vessels (vanishing testis) or intra-abdominal localization.
Fowler-Stephens orchiopexy (single-stage or two-stage) divides the testicular vessels, relying on collateral blood supply from the deferential (vasal) artery and cremasteric vessels.
Undescended testes carry a 4- to 8-fold increased lifetime risk of testicular malignancy (seminoma being most common); orchidopexy facilitates clinical examination but does not eliminate risk.
Patent processus vaginalis is present in over 90% of cryptorchid testes, requiring high dissection and ligation of the hernia sac during open or laparoscopic orchidopexy.
Bilateral non-palpable testes with normal male genitalia requires immediate urgent evaluation for 46,XX congenital adrenal hyperplasia (salt-wasting crisis risk), karyotype, and hCG stimulation test.
Hormonal therapy with hCG or GnRH agonists is not routinely recommended for cryptorchidism due to low efficacy (<15% durable descent) and adverse effects on future germ cells.

modules.name: Vesicoureteral Reflux and Deflux Injection

topics.title: Vesicoureteral Reflux (VUR): Grading, Renal Scarring, Cohen Reimplantation and Deflux
topics.book: Campbell-Walsh-Wein Urology 12e Ch 46 (Vesicoureteral Reflux)

mustKnow.fact: Vesicoureteral reflux (VUR) is classified by the International Reflux Study into Grades I to V on voiding cystourethrography (VCUG), with Grade V showing severe caliceal blunting and gross tortuosity.
Primary VUR results from congenital deficiency of the intravesical submucosal ureteral tunnel; a normal tunnel length-to-diameter ratio of 5:1 provides passive anti-reflux flap-valve competence.
99mTc-DMSA (dimercaptosuccinic acid) renal cortical scintigraphy represents the gold standard modality for detecting renal parenchymal scarring, focal defects, and differential renal function.
Endoscopic subureteral transurethral injection (STING / HIT technique) of dextranomer/hyaluronic acid copolymer (Deflux) achieves 75% to 85% reflux resolution for Grades II to IV.
Cohen cross-trigonal ureteral reimplantation creates a lengthened submucosal tunnel across the trigone to the opposite bladder wall with open/robotic success rates exceeding 95% to 98%.
Leadbetter-Politano reimplantation enters the bladder extravesically and brings the ureter through a new, higher hiatus, preserving normal anatomical orientation for future endoscopic access.
Lich-Gregoir extravesical ureteral reimplantation incises the detrusor muscle down to intact mucosa without entering the bladder lumen, eliminating gross hematuria and reducing bladder spasms.
Bladder and bowel dysfunction (BBD, dysfunctional elimination syndrome) significantly decreases spontaneous VUR resolution and doubles surgical failure rates; treatment of constipation is essential.

modules.name: Posterior Urethral Valves and Obstructive Uropathy

topics.title: Posterior Urethral Valves (PUV): Antenatal Detection, Endoscopic Ablation and Valve Bladder
topics.book: Campbell-Walsh-Wein Urology 12e Ch 47 (Posterior Urethral Valves and Congenital Urethral Anomalies)

mustKnow.fact: Posterior urethral valves (PUV) represent the most common cause of congenital severe lower urinary tract obstruction in male neonates, occurring in 1 in 4000 to 8000 live births.
Antenatal ultrasound features of PUV include bilateral hydroureteronephrosis, thick-walled trabeculated bladder, oligohydramnios, and keyhole sign (dilated posterior urethra).

Young classification: Type I valves (95% of cases) are obstructing mucosal folds extending distally from the verumontanum to the lateral bulbar urethra; Type III is a disc-like diaphragm with central perforation.

Initial neonatal stabilization requires placement of a 5F or 6F feeding tube or catheter (avoiding large balloon catheters) to decompress the urinary tract, alongside aggressive fluid/electrolyte resuscitation.
Definitive primary treatment is transurethral endoscopic valve ablation (using cold knife, Bugbee electrocautery, or Holmium laser) at the 5, 7, and 12 o'clock positions.
VURD syndrome (Posterior Urethral Valves, Unilateral Reflux, and Dysplasia) acts as a pressure release mechanism protecting the contralateral kidney from elevated intravesical pressures.
Valve bladder syndrome describes secondary chronic bladder dysfunction characterized by poor compliance, detrusor overactivity, and myogenic failure resulting in persistent upper tract dilatation.
Nadir serum creatinine under 0.8 mg/dL (70 micromol/L) within the first year of life represents the single most significant predictor of favorable long-term renal function in PUV.

modules.name: Bladder Exstrophy and Epispadias Complex

topics.title: Bladder Exstrophy-Epispadias Complex (BEEC): Staged Reconstruction and Kelly Procedure
topics.book: Campbell-Walsh-Wein Urology 12e Ch 48 (Exstrophy-Epispadias Complex)

mustKnow.fact: Bladder exstrophy results from failure of the cloacal membrane to be reinforced by ingrowth of lateral mesoderm, followed by premature rupture of the unstable membrane before the 6th gestational week.
Anatomical defects comprise open exposed bladder template, splayed pubic symphysis (widened pubic diastasis), divergent rectus abdominis muscles, epispadias, and low-set umbilicus.

Classic staged repair: primary bladder and abdominal wall closure with bilateral pelvic osteotomy in first 72 hours; epispadias repair at 1 to 2 years; bladder neck reconstruction (Young-Dees-Leadbetter) at 4 to 5 years.
Bilateral pelvic osteotomy (posterior iliac, anterior innominate, or horizontal periacetabular) is mandatory in patients closed beyond 72 hours to re-approximate pubic bones without tension.
Complete Primary Repair of Exstrophy (CPRE / Mitchell technique) simultaneously accomplishes bladder closure, epispadias repair, and bladder neck reconstruction in the neonatal period.
Kelly procedure achieves anatomical reconstruction of the bladder neck, pelvic floor, and external sphincter complex, restoring anatomical continence without necessitating bladder neck tightening.
Bladder capacity of at least 85 mL to 100 mL under anesthesia is an absolute prerequisite prior to undergoing formal bladder neck reconstruction to ensure voluntary voiding continence.
Patients with unclosed or reconstructed bladder exstrophy face a lifelong 400-fold increased risk of bladder adenocarcinoma, originating from glandular metaplasia (cystitis glandularis).

modules.name: Duplex Collecting Systems and Ureteroceles

topics.title: Duplex Collecting Systems: Weigert-Meyer Law, Ectopic Ureters and Ureterocele Decompression
topics.book: Campbell-Walsh-Wein Urology 12e Ch 45 (Anomalies of the Upper Urinary Tract)

mustKnow.fact: Weigert-Meyer law dictates duplex kidney anatomy: upper pole ureter enters bladder ectopically inferomedial to normal and is prone to obstruction/ureterocele; lower pole ureter enters superolaterally and refluxes.
Ureterocele is a cystic dilation of the terminal intravesical submucosal ureter, classified as intravesical (orthotopic, confined to bladder) or ectopic (extending into bladder neck or urethra).
Cobra head sign (spring onion sign) on intravenous urography shows a radiopaque round filling defect surrounded by a thin radiolucent halo within the contrast-filled bladder.

Endoscopic transurethral puncture/incision (puncture with Bugbee electrode, cold knife, or laser) is the initial decompression of choice in obstructing ureteroceles, especially in neonates with sepsis.

Ectopic ureter in females can insert distal to the external urinary sphincter (into urethra, vagina, vestibule, or uterus), producing pathognomonic continuous urinary dribbling despite normal voiding cycles.
Ectopic ureter in males always inserts proximal to the external sphincter (into posterior urethra, seminal vesicle, vas deferens, or ejaculatory duct), never causing urinary incontinence.
Laparoscopic or robotic heminephroureterectomy (upper pole excision) is the definitive surgical standard when the upper moiety is non-functioning or dysplastic (<10% split function).

Ipsilateral ureteroureterostomy (anastomosing obstructed upper pole ureter to functioning lower pole ureter) preserves renal parenchyma without requiring pelvic dissection in functioning duplex systems.

modules.name: Prune Belly Syndrome and Urachal Disorders

topics.title: Prune Belly Syndrome (Eagle-Barrett) and Urachal Remnants (Urachal Cyst, Sinus and Carcinoma)
topics.book: Campbell-Walsh-Wein Urology 12e Ch 49-50 (Abdominal Wall Defects and Urachal Anomalies)

mustKnow.fact: Prune belly syndrome (Eagle-Barrett syndrome) comprises the classic triad: deficient abdominal wall musculature, bilateral cryptorchidism, and dilated tortuous urinary tract (megacystis-megaureter).
Prostatic hypoplasia with dilated posterior urethra is characteristic of prune belly syndrome, causing functional urinary stasis without mechanical posterior urethral valves.
Comprehensive surgical reconstruction (Monfort abdominal wall plication combined with bilateral transabdominal orchiopexy and selective ureteral tapering/reimplantation) is performed in infancy.
Patent urachus (50% of congenital urachal anomalies) results from complete failure of the allantoic duct to obliterate, presenting with continuous clear urine drainage from the umbilicus.
Urachal cyst (30%) arises when both ends of the allantoic canal close while the central segment remains patent, commonly presenting as an infected infraumbilical midline suprapubic mass.
Urachal sinus presents with intermittent purulent or serosanguinous discharge from an umbilicus with a blind-ending tract extending toward the bladder dome.
Urachal carcinoma is an aggressive adenocarcinoma arising from intestinal metaplasia in the urachus at the bladder dome, accounting for <0.5% of all bladder cancers.
Surgical treatment of urachal carcinoma mandates en bloc partial cystectomy with complete excision of the urachus, median umbilical ligament, and umbilicus.

modules.name: Disorders of Sex Development (DSD) and Ambiguous Genitalia

topics.title: Disorders of Sex Development: Diagnostic Algorithms, Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia and Genitoplasty
topics.book: Campbell-Walsh-Wein Urology 12e Ch 51 (Disorders of Sex Development)

mustKnow.fact: Disorders of sex development (DSD) are categorized into 46,XX DSD, 46,XY DSD, and sex chromosome DSD (such as 45,X/46,XY mixed gonadal dysgenesis).
Congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH, 21-hydroxylase deficiency, CYP21A2 mutation) is the most common cause of ambiguous genitalia in neonates, classified as 46,XX DSD with severe salt wasting.

Prader staging (Stages I to V) quantifies the degree of virilization in 46,XX CAH females, ranging from mild clitoromegaly (Stage I) to completely virilized phallic urethra with fused scrotum (Stage V).

Complete androgen insensitivity syndrome (CAIS, 46,XY DSD) is caused by androgen receptor gene mutations; patients have female external genitalia, blind vaginal pouch, absent uterus, and abdominal/inguinal testes.

5-alpha reductase deficiency (46,XY DSD, SRD5A2 mutation) features pseudovaginal perineoscrotal hypospadias at birth, with marked virilization and phallic growth at puberty driven by rising testosterone.
Gonadal malignancy risk is highest in patients with intra-abdominal dysgenetic gonads containing Y-chromosomal material (GBY region), mandating early prophylactic gonadectomy.
Total or partial urogenital mobilization (PUM / TUM) mobilizes the confluence of the urethra and vagina as a single unit to the perineum, avoiding separate vaginal flap dissection.
Nerve-sparing clitoroplasty meticulously dissects the dorsal neurovascular bundle away from the erectile tissue, preserving clitoral sensation while recessing or reducing glans volume.

sections.name: Genitourinary Infections, Adrenals, Renal Failure and Transplantation

modules.name: Renal Infections: Pyelonephritis and Perinephric Abscess

topics.title: Severe Renal Infections: Acute Pyelonephritis, Renal Abscess and Emphysematous Pyelonephritis
topics.book: Campbell-Walsh-Wein Urology 12e Ch 55 (Infections of the Urinary Tract)

mustKnow.fact: Acute uncomplicated pyelonephritis is predominantly caused by uropathogenic Escherichia coli (>80%), characterized by fever, flank pain, costovertebral angle tenderness, and pyuria.

Emphysematous pyelonephritis (EPN) is a necrotizing gas-producing infection occurring almost exclusively in diabetic patients (over 90%), with E. coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae producing tissue gas via glucose fermentation.

Huang-Tseng CT classification of EPN: Class 1 (gas in collecting system only), Class 2 (parenchymal gas without extrarenal extension), Class 3A (perirenal extension), Class 3B (pararenal extension), Class 4 (bilateral or solitary kidney).
Management of EPN shifted from emergency nephrectomy to prompt percutaneous catheter drainage (PCD) combined with intravenous broad-spectrum antibiotics, preserving renal parenchyma in >80%.

Xanthogranulomatous pyelonephritis (XPN) is an aggressive chronic destructive granulomatous infection characterized by lipid-laden foamy macrophages (xanthoma cells), commonly associated with a staghorn calculus.
Bear paw sign on contrast CT scan in XPN depicts multiple rounded low-attenuation dilated calices resembling a paw print, surrounded by thinned, non-enhancing renal parenchyma.

Renal cortical abscess (renal carbuncle) classically develops via hematogenous seeding of Staphylococcus aureus from a distant cutaneous focus; managed with targeted intravenous antibiotics or percutaneous drainage if >3 cm.

Obstructive pyelonephritis with hydronephrosis secondary to an obstructing calculus is a urological emergency mandating immediate emergent decompression via retrograde ureteral stent or percutaneous nephrostomy.

modules.name: Genitourinary Tuberculosis and Fungal Infections

topics.title: Genitourinary Tuberculosis: Putty Kidney, Thimble Bladder and Fungal Bezoars
topics.book: Campbell-Walsh-Wein Urology 12e Ch 60 (Tuberculosis and Parasitic Infections of the GU Tract)

mustKnow.fact: Genitourinary tuberculosis (GUTB) is caused by metastatic hematogenous dissemination of Mycobacterium tuberculosis from a primary pulmonary focus to renal cortical glomeruli and peritubular capillaries.
Sterile pyuria (presence of white blood cells in urine with repeatedly negative routine bacterial cultures) is the classic hallmark presentation of urinary tuberculosis.
Kerr's kink (stepladder or corkscrew ureter) represents multi-segmental strictures and fibrosis along the ureter caused by transmural caseating granulomatous inflammation.

Thimble bladder (contracted, fibrotic bladder with low capacity <50 mL to 100 mL) results from profound muscular scarring, requiring enterocystoplasty (bladder augmentation) once medical cure is verified.
Putty kidney (cement kidney) refers to complete autonephrectomy wherein caseous necrosis and calcification completely replace and devitalize the renal parenchyma.
Standard medical treatment of GUTB consists of a 6-month regimen of antitubercular therapy (2 months of isoniazid, rifampin, pyrazinamide, ethambutol followed by 4 months of isoniazid and rifampin).
Fungal balls (Candida albicans bezoars) develop in the renal pelvis of diabetic or immunocompromised patients, causing mechanical upper tract obstruction.
Management of obstructing fungal bezoars requires surgical or endourological debulking, continuous local irrigation with amphotericin B (50 mg/L sterile water), and systemic fluconazole therapy.

modules.name: Fournier Gangrene and Urogenital Sepsis

topics.title: Fournier Gangrene: Pathogenesis, Surgical Debridement and Urosepsis Protocols
topics.book: Campbell-Walsh-Wein Urology 12e Ch 55-56 (Genitourinary Infections and Fournier Gangrene)

mustKnow.fact: Fournier gangrene is a rapidly progressive polymicrobial necrotizing fasciitis of the perineal, perianal, and external genital regions, typically combining aerobic and anaerobic bacteria synergistically.
Endarteritis obliterans caused by bacterial toxins results in microvascular thrombosis of subcutaneous vessels, leading to extensive tissue necrosis advancing up to 2 cm to 3 cm per hour.

The testes are characteristically spared from necrosis in Fournier gangrene because their blood supply originates directly from the aorta via testicular arteries, distinct from perineal fascial supply.
Immediate, aggressive, radical surgical debridement of all necrotic tissue until viable bleeding margins are reached is the single most critical determinant of survival.

Fournier Gangrene Severity Index (FGSI) evaluates 9 physiological parameters (temperature, heart rate, respiration, sodium, potassium, creatinine, hematocrit, leukocyte count, bicarbonate); score >9 predicts >75% mortality.

Broad-spectrum empiric antimicrobial coverage must cover MRSA, gram-negative coliforms, Pseudomonas, and anaerobes (e.g., piperacillin-tazobactam plus vancomycin plus clindamycin to inhibit toxin synthesis).
Urinary diversion via suprapubic catheterization or urethral catheter and fecal diversion via diverting colostomy or fecal management system prevent ongoing wound contamination.

Urosepsis requires urgent resuscitation adhering to Surviving Sepsis guidelines: 30 mL/kg crystalloids within 3 hours, blood cultures, broad-spectrum IV antibiotics within 1 hour, and urgent surgical source control.

modules.name: Prostatitis Syndromes and Male Accessory Gland Infections

topics.title: Prostatitis Syndromes (NIH Categories I-IV): Acute Bacterial, Chronic Pelvic Pain and Scrotal Abscess
topics.book: Campbell-Walsh-Wein Urology 12e Ch 56 (Inflammatory Conditions of the Male Genitourinary Tract)

mustKnow.fact: NIH Prostatitis Classification: Category I (acute bacterial prostatitis), Category II (chronic bacterial prostatitis), Category III (chronic pelvic pain syndrome, IIIA inflammatory, IIIB non-inflammatory), Category IV (asymptomatic inflammatory).

Category I acute bacterial prostatitis presents with high fever, chills, perineal pain, and severe LUTS; vigorous digital rectal examination is strictly contraindicated due to risk of precipitating bacteremia and urosepsis.
Transurethral catheterization is contraindicated in acute urinary retention secondary to acute bacterial prostatitis; decompression must be accomplished via a fine percutaneous suprapubic cystostomy.

Category II chronic bacterial prostatitis requires fluoroquinolones (ciprofloxacin 500 mg twice daily) or trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole for 4 to 6 weeks to penetrate the lipid barrier of the uninflamed prostatic epithelium.

Meares-Stamey four-glass localization test compares quantitative bacterial cultures and microscopy of initial urine (VB1), midstream urine (VB2), expressed prostatic secretions (EPS), and post-massage urine (VB3).

Prostatic abscess commonly complicates uncontrolled prostatitis in diabetic or immunocompromised patients, diagnosed via transrectal ultrasound (TRUS) or pelvic CT showing a multilocular fluid collection.
Treatment of prostatic abscess measuring >1.5 cm to 2 cm involves transrectal or transperineal ultrasound-guided needle aspiration or transurethral unroofing (TURP unroofing).
Urethral caruncle in females presents as a painful, bleeding, benign polypoid vascular mass at the posterior lip of the external urethral meatus, treated primarily with topical estrogen cream.

modules.name: Adrenal Tumours, Incidentaloma and Pheochromocytoma

topics.title: Adrenal Surgical Disorders: Incidentaloma, Pheochromocytoma, Cushing Syndrome and Adrenalectomy
topics.book: Campbell-Walsh-Wein Urology 12e Ch 105-107 (Surgery of the Adrenal Glands)

mustKnow.fact: Adrenal incidentaloma is an unsuspected adrenal mass discovered on cross-sectional imaging performed for non-adrenal indications; functional evaluation for hypercortisolemia, pheochromocytoma, and aldosteronism is mandatory.
